description:
Goal

A demanded callable TransportShape(position) determines the function/value representation once from exact upstream facts and products. That revision-relative product answer is the authority consumed by ABI, backend, interpreter, and native layers; none of them reselect, reconstruct, or reinterpret callable identity or layout.

North-star contract

- Artifact work is product-keyed and request-local. One product produces from named current fact/product prerequisites or returns exact waits.
- Completion is explicit: when all prerequisites requested by that product have produced for the revisions it reads, that answer may settle. A closure-wide no-change sweep is not completion evidence.
- A producer may settle a dependency group internally only when a real cycle requires it. It publishes the requested revision-relative answer, not an eagerly projected inventory.
- RootBackendProduct only densifies symbolic products already demanded into the request-local inventory.
- Transport owns the physical callable/function determination. Lower layers consume its product and never relitigate it.

Proven current mismatch

- Runtime demand records each call argument under an exact callee ExecutableKey plus semantic input slot before transport. Per-producer CallableFlowFact carries function, captures, direct/public surfaces, exact resolutions, and semantic input mappings.
- project_executable_input_source projects those sources into ShapeIds, then callable_input_shapes_for_demand compares them against a joined physical rendering of CallableDemand and decides producer eligibility again. Paired Enum.drop_while proves the universal physical comparison rejects valid producers. Existential physical matching admits an untargeted same-layout producer. Physical shape is therefore not semantic selection authority.
- Replacing that comparison with target/edge matching inside transport is also wrong: it repeats an upstream relation decision instead of refining the product inputs already named. The earlier spike at 2e4f39973 is retained only as a negative proof that physical reselection is unsound.
- TransportComponent(position) currently invokes solve_transport_closure: it expands an executable set to a no-change fixpoint, waits on the set, projects every member, solves every component, and records all callable/boundary facts. This was ported from the legacy whole-transport projection and later cached once per closure for performance. Being request-triggered and cached does not by itself make it a narrow product producer.
- IncomingInputSlot currently snapshots the session source vector. Its safety depends on the surrounding closure expansion forcing OutgoingInputEdges products before the snapshot; the slot product does not itself carry an explicit contributor/completion domain. Whether that is sufficient under every product schedule is not yet proven.

Spike gate before implementation

1. Work one minimal callable input on paper from requested ProductKey through exact facts/products to the required transport answer. Name the semantic relation, physical decision, and final consumer-visible result.
2. Trace paired drop_while through production product request/production telemetry. Record which TransportShape/Component, RuntimeDemand, OutgoingInputEdges, IncomingInputSlot, CallableFacts, and BoundaryFacts products are requested, waited on, produced, invalidated, and consumed.
3. Prove or falsify that an IncomingInputSlot/TransportShape can be observed before every demanded contributor has produced, using schedule permutations through the production driver. A later invalidation is not permission to publish a partial answer to a consumer.
4. Measure what one TransportComponent request causes solve_transport_closure to project beyond the requested dependency component. Distinguish a necessary cyclic settlement from pass-shaped overproduction.
5. Locate the smallest existing authority that knows the exact producer/use set and the exact completion condition. If information is absent, identify the missing named fact/product; do not infer it from World scans, shapes, Ty, debug order, or sibling inventories.
6. Only after those proofs, define the monotone refinement from that authority to the callable TransportShape/CallableFacts/BoundaryFacts answers and identify the closure projection, selector, fallback, caches, tests, and docs that can be deleted.

Signal

- The spike shows an explicit requested-product DAG and a schedule-independent completion proof for the minimal example.
- Every produced callable transport answer is justified by named prerequisites; no unrequested closure inventory is used as authority.
- Paired drop_while retains both valid producer/use relations without a physical eligibility test.
- A same-physical-layout distinct-target case cannot cross-select because the exact relation is preserved, not reconstructed.
- Lower layers consume the produced function/ABI decision without semantic or physical reselection.
- Tests assert product requests, exact waits, production, invalidation, and consumer-visible behavior rather than a private closure representation.

Scope

No production implementation begins until the spike proves both the dependency boundary and completion condition. The remaining projected-source Unknown stays blocked here until this authority is known. The uncalled first-class path discrepancy remains fz-k22.31. fz-k22.29 owns lazy direct invocation only after this ticket establishes the product authority it may consume.
title: Make callable transport determination a product-owned refinement
